newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM attacks Bhutto's electricity policy.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM attacks Bhutto's electricity policy.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday attacked former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's policy of promoting private electricity generation and said his government would try to renegotiate lower tariffs with private plants.
State utilities were struggling to pay higher electricity charges, he said during a visit to Karachi.
"It is the wrong power policy of the previous government from which we are suffering now," Sharif told reporters.

Bhutto's government, seeking to attract foreign investment, issued letters of support between 1994 and 1996 for almost 3,200 megawatts of new capacity at a guaranteed payment of 6.5 cents per unit for the first 10 years.

Almost all the projects, built with foreign investment, are expected to come on stream by the end of 1998 and officials say the state-run Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) and the Karachi Electric Supply Corp (KESC) will have to raise more than $1.27 billion to buy electricity generated by the private companies.
"WAPDA and KESC are already in trouble," Sharif said. "How are they going to pay these high tariffs?"
Sharif said state utilities were already in a bad financial shape and burdening them with additional liabilities would push them into insolvency.
"We are working on this issue. We will try to bring them down," Sharif said when asked if the government would renegotiate the tariffs earlier agreed with the private power plants.
